teacher_request.learning_goal: Understand force, motion and engineering design.

output.interpreted_goal: Explore how forces affect motion and use engineering design through building, testing, and revising mechanisms or structures.

choices.educational_reasoning: Varying the catapult setup offers a direct way to compare how changes in applied force relate to motion. Students can make predictions, observe launches, and discuss which design choices may affect the result.

Designing and testing a track connects engineering decisions—such as shaping a banked curve—with the motion of a marble. Students can investigate what keeps it on track and refine their design based on observations.

Building an adjustable-vane windmill and testing how it lifts weight links design choices to motion and mechanical performance. Students can compare settings and reason about how speed, gearing, and power relate.
